personality: Stout, cheerful and a dangerous swordsman. He prays well, eats better and fights best of all.
voice: Thou art a lusty fellow, and I like thee well.

cards.title: The Curtal Friar
cards.text: Robin heard of a friar of Fountains Abbey who could draw a long bow and swing a sword as well as any man. He found him sitting by a stream and made him carry him across on his back. Then the friar made Robin carry him back again, and when Robin demanded a third ride, the friar tipped him off midstream into the water.

source.work: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
source.author: Howard Pyle, 1883
source.chapter: Robin Hood Seeketh the Curtal Friar

cards.title: Dogs and Bowmen
cards.text: They fought with swords from morning until the sun was high, and neither could best the other. Robin blew his horn and his yeomen came running. The friar whistled, and a pack of great dogs came bounding out of the trees. Only Little John's quick arrows saved Robin's men from being torn.

source.work: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
source.author: Howard Pyle, 1883
source.chapter: Robin Hood Seeketh the Curtal Friar

cards.title: The Chaplain of Sherwood
cards.text: Robin offered him a place in the band, with a full belly and good company, and the friar was glad to come. He became the merry chaplain of Sherwood, and when Allan a Dale's true love was about to be married against her will, it was the friar who married her to Allan instead.

source.work: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
source.author: Howard Pyle, 1883
source.chapter: Robin Hood and Allan a Dale
